topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: I remember the day I planted that little sapling, the soil cooler than I expected, the air fragrant with earth and spring. Each year, I watched it grow, a silent witness to my own changes. When I heard it was gone, a part of me felt adrift, like the shade it once provided. But then, I recalled the joy of every leaf, every branch. Its legacy isn’t just in the wood; it’s in the memories, the lessons in patience and care. I can still honor it by planting another, letting the cycle of growth and change continue, just as it did before.
